overview.title: Admin overview
overview.description: Manage accounts, watch hosts, sandboxes and operations across every owner, and set deployment policy.
overview.policy: Sign-up is {{signup}}. 2FA for admins: {{admins}}. 2FA for everyone else: {{others}}.

setup.title: Deployment setup
setup.description: What this server is configured with. Values are never shown here; each item is set in the server's environment unless it says otherwise.
setup.docsPath: Environment variables: {{path}} in the WS Sandbox Proxy source repository.
setup.unknown: Couldn't load this status. Reload the page to try again.

email.title: Email (SMTP)
email.ok: SMTP settings are present. Sign-up verification, password resets and invitations are sent by email.
email.missing: Not configured. Nobody can verify an email address, so new accounts (yours included) can't sign in, and invitations and password resets aren't sent. Set SMTP_HOST and SMTP_FROM.

imageStore.title: Image store
imageStore.s3: S3 image store. Templates, community bases and offloaded disks are kept in your bucket.
imageStore.peer: No S3 bucket: hosts copy template images from each other, so a template is only as available as the hosts that hold it, and disk offload is off. Set the IMAGE_S3_* variables.
imageStore.off: Image distribution is off (IMAGE_DISTRIBUTION=off): no template builds or community bases.

dataKey.title: Data encryption key
dataKey.ok: Set. Webhooks, CLI logins and preview tunnels can store their secrets.
dataKey.missing: Not set. Webhooks, CLI logins and preview tunnels stay off. Set DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY (64 hex characters, the same on server and worker).

backups.title: Database backups
backups.optional: Off (optional). Turn on with BACKUP_ENABLED and a backup bucket; see the backup guide.
backups.problem: On, but the latest backup is missing, late or failing.
backups.unknown: On, but no backup result has been recorded yet.

tunnels.title: Preview tunnels
tunnels.optional: Off (optional). Lets sandboxes share declared ports through short-lived links.

users.title: Users
users.description: Invite people, change roles, archive or restore accounts, and delete accounts that no longer own anything.
users.inviteDescription: Creates an account with a temporary password and emails the sign-in details. On their first sign-in the person gets a link to confirm their email address, so email (SMTP) must be configured on this server.
users.revealEmailedDescription: {{email}} has been emailed a temporary password. You can also copy it below if needed.
users.revealNotEmailedDescription: The account for {{email}} was created, but the email could not be sent. Share the temporary password with them through another channel.
users.tempPasswordHint: This password is only shown once. On their first sign-in the person confirms their email address through the link they're sent, then signs in again. They should change the password afterwards.
users.deleteDescription: This permanently removes the account with its sessions, credentials, SDK keys, templates and finished sandbox and operation records. It is refused while the account still has hosts, sandboxes, unfinished operations, pending events or active transfers. To keep the account but block access, archive it instead.
users.typeEmailToConfirm: Type the user's email to confirm
users.deleteBlockedHint: The account keeps working until these are gone. Ask the owner to delete their hosts and sandboxes, or wait for in-flight work to finish, then try again.

confirm.promoteDescription: Administrators can manage every account, see metadata for every owner's hosts, sandboxes and operations, and change deployment policy. They must use two-factor authentication while it is required for administrators.
confirm.demoteDescription: They lose the admin area immediately. Their own hosts, sandboxes and keys are not affected. The last active administrator can't be demoted.
confirm.archiveDescription: They are signed out everywhere and can't sign in. Their SDK keys and host credentials stop working and connected hosts are disconnected. Their hosts, sandboxes and data are kept, and restoring the account lets them sign in again.

observability.title: Observability
observability.description: Metadata across every owner: hosts, sandboxes and operations by id, state and time, plus maintenance status. Commands, output, files and credentials are never shown here.

filters.invalidId: IDs use only letters, digits, - and _.
filters.fixToSearch: Fix the highlighted filter to see results.

maintenance.queuesDescription: Background job counts for each maintenance queue.
maintenance.noneFailedDescription: The maintenance queues have no retained failed jobs. This list refreshes automatically while open.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Deployment-wide sign-up and two-factor policy, and the limits this deployment enforces.
settings.securityDescription: Applies to every account. Each change asks for confirmation first.
settings.force2faAdminWarning: You must enable 2FA for your own account before you can require it for others.
settings.recoveryNote: Your own password, second factor and backup codes are managed in your account's security settings, not here.

force2faInternalUsers.title: Require 2FA for administrators
force2faInternalUsers.description: Required by default. Administrators without a second factor lose the admin area once their 24-hour enrollment window after sign-up has passed.

force2faPublicUsers.title: Require 2FA for everyone else
force2faPublicUsers.description: Non-admin accounts must set up a second factor. Until they do, the dashboard and their SDK keys and host credentials are refused once their enrollment window has passed.

signupEnabled.title: Open sign-up
signupEnabled.description: Lets anyone create an account from the sign-up page. When off, accounts are created only by invitation (and the configured admin emails).

force2faInternalUsers.onDescription: Administrators without a second factor will lose the admin area once their enrollment window has passed.
force2faInternalUsers.offDescription: Administrator accounts will be protected by a password alone. A stolen password would then give full control of this deployment. Only do this if you have a strong reason.

force2faPublicUsers.onDescription: Accounts older than 24 hours without a second factor are refused at once — including their SDK keys and host credentials — until they enroll. Tell your users before you turn this on.
force2faPublicUsers.offDescription: Non-admin accounts will be able to use the dashboard, SDK keys and hosts with a password alone.

signupEnabled.onDescription: Anyone who can reach this deployment will be able to create an account and enroll hosts.
signupEnabled.offDescription: New accounts will be created only by invitation. Existing accounts are not affected.

force2faInternalUsers.on: Two-factor authentication is now required for administrators
force2faInternalUsers.off: Two-factor authentication is no longer required for administrators

force2faPublicUsers.on: Two-factor authentication is now required for everyone
force2faPublicUsers.off: Two-factor authentication is no longer required for non-admin accounts

offloadGrace.title: Offloaded disk copies
offloadGrace.description: After an offloaded sandbox starts again, its copy in the image store is kept this long as a salvage window, then deleted. The copy is never restored automatically.
offloadGrace.label: Keep the copy for (seconds)
offloadGrace.hint: 0 deletes it as soon as the sandbox is running; at most 604800 (7 days). The default is 3600 (1 hour).
offloadGrace.invalid: Enter a whole number of seconds from 0 to 604800.

tunnel.title: Preview tunnels (optional)
tunnel.description: Connect a tunnel server so sandboxes can share declared ports through short-lived links. The host runs the tunnel client outside the VM; nothing is installed in the guest. Without a tunnel server everything else works unchanged, and tunnel API calls answer that tunnels are not configured.
tunnel.loadFailed: The tunnel server setting could not be loaded.
tunnel.statusOff: Not configured: preview tunnels are off.
tunnel.keyMissing: Set DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY on the server to store a tunnel credential.
tunnel.urlHint: The server's https:// origin, for example https://tunnel.example.com.
tunnel.urlInvalid: Enter an https:// origin without a path.
tunnel.credentialHint: A tnsvc_ credential created on the tunnel server with tunnel-server service add. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
tunnel.credentialKeep: The server and credential stay as configured; only the limit can change here. For another server or credential, turn tunnels off, wait until the setting is gone, then configure it.
tunnel.credentialInvalid: A service credential starts with tnsvc_.
tunnel.maxHint: How many sandboxes of one account may have a tunnel at once (1 to 1000).
tunnel.maxInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 1000.
tunnel.confirmDescription: Tunnel calls are refused at once. Every sandbox tunnel is then deleted on the tunnel server, every link stops working, and the stored credential is removed.

refused.url_invalid: The URL must be an https:// origin without a path.
refused.key_missing: Set DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY on the server first.
refused.credential_invalid: A service credential starts with tnsvc_.
refused.credential_rejected: The tunnel server rejected this credential.
refused.server_unreachable: The tunnel server could not be reached over HTTPS.
refused.turning_off: Tunnels are turning off. Wait until the setting disappears, then configure again.
refused.turn_off_first: The server and credential cannot change while configured. Turn tunnels off, wait until the setting is gone, then configure the new server or credential.

tunnel.statusTurningOff: Turning off: deleting {{total}} tunnels. The setting disappears when they are gone.
tunnel.turningOff: Turning off preview tunnels: every tunnel is being deleted.
tunnel.removeNowTitle: Remove the tunnel server setting now?
tunnel.removeNowDescription: Use this only if the tunnel server is gone for good. wssp forgets every tunnel at once; tunnels still on the tunnel server stop when their 7-day lifetime ends.

settings.limitsDescription: Set by the deployment's configuration and read-only here.

problems.selfDemotion: You can't remove your own admin role. Ask another administrator to do it.
problems.selfArchive: You can't archive your own account.
problems.selfDelete: You can't delete your own account from the admin area. Use your account settings instead.
problems.lastAdmin: This is the last active administrator. Promote someone else first, so the deployment always has an administrator.
problems.userNotFound: That account no longer exists. The list has been refreshed.
problems.emailTaken: An account with that email already exists.
problems.inviteRefused: The auth configuration refused to create this account. Ask whoever deploys this app to check the invite setup.
problems.ownTwoFactorRequired: Turn on two-factor authentication for your own account before requiring it of others.
problems.signupEmailRequired: Sign-up sends a verification email, and this deployment has no email delivery configured. Ask whoever deploys this app to set up SMTP first.
problems.deletionBlocked: Nothing was deleted. The account still has live resources:
problems.deletionChanged: The account's resources changed while it was being deleted, and nothing blocks it now. Try again.
problems.accessLost: That action is no longer available. Reload the page.
problems.invalid: The server rejected that request. Check the values and try again.
problems.rateLimited: Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.

blockers.shared_pool_workloads: Shared pool workloads still need access-loss evaluation. Delete the pools and wait for cleanup before retrying.
blockers.hosts: Enrolled hosts — the owner must delete them first.
blockers.sandboxes: Sandboxes that are not deleted yet.
blockers.outbox: Pending events that have not been delivered yet.
blockers.transfers: File transfers that are still in progress.
blockers.image_jobs: Image downloads, uploads or template captures that are still in progress.

backups.title: Database backups

state.fresh_one: Newest backup is {{count}} hour old (limit {{limit}} hours).
state.fresh_other: Newest backup is {{count}} hours old (limit {{limit}} hours).
state.stale_one: Newest backup is {{count}} hour old — older than the {{limit}} hour limit. The backup job is not producing dumps.
state.stale_other: Newest backup is {{count}} hours old — older than the {{limit}} hour limit. The backup job is not producing dumps.
state.empty: No backups found in the bucket yet.
state.error: Could not read the backup bucket.
state.misconfigured: Backups are turned on but set up incorrectly, so none are being taken.
state.setupMissing: Backups are turned on but the off-site bucket is not configured yet.
state.unknown: No freshness check has run yet. The worker records one every 6 hours.

reason.futureTimestamp: The newest backup is dated in the future, so its age cannot be trusted. The clock on the machine that made it is probably wrong.

backups.docsHint: If backups are missing or out of date, ask whoever deploys this app to set them up — you cannot enable them from here.

twoFactorNudge.title: Two-factor authentication is not set up
twoFactorNudge.message: Your admin account signs in with a password alone. Add an authenticator app as a second factor so a stolen password can't unlock this dashboard.
twoFactorNudge.requiredTitle: Two-factor authentication is required for your admin account
twoFactorNudge.requiredMessage: Add an authenticator app as a second factor {{deadline}}. After that, this dashboard stays locked until you finish enrolling.
twoFactorNudge.blockedTitle: Admin access is locked until you set up two-factor authentication
twoFactorNudge.blockedMessage: Your enrollment window has closed, so admin actions are being refused. Set up an authenticator app now to get this dashboard back.
twoFactorNudge.configurable: An admin who has already enrolled can change this policy under Settings in the admin dashboard.

imageQuota.title: Image quotas for {{name}}
imageQuota.description: Overrides only lower the deployment limit; the smaller value applies.
imageQuota.loadFailed: Couldn't load this account's image quotas.
imageQuota.blankHint: Leave empty to use the deployment limit.
imageQuota.invalidStored: Enter a whole number from 0 to 1048576, or leave it empty.
imageQuota.invalidDownloads: Enter a whole number from 0 to 100000, or leave it empty.
imageQuota.invalidConcurrent: Enter a whole number from 0 to 1000, or leave it empty.
imageQuota.invalidMinutes: Enter a whole number from 0 to 1000000, or leave it empty.
imageQuota.offloadHint: Offloaded stopped-sandbox disks in the image store. Leave empty to use the deployment limit; 0 stops new offloads (disks stay on their hosts).

dataKey.title: Data encryption key
dataKey.description: Which root key new encrypted data is sealed under, how many rows each key still holds, and the return keys hosts seal login captures to. Key ids only; key values never reach this page.
dataKey.loadFailed: Failed to load the data-key status.
dataKey.notConfigured: DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set on this server: webhooks and CLI logins are off.
dataKey.noEpoch: No encrypted data has been written yet.
dataKey.promoteDescription: Every new encrypted write will be sealed under {{kid}}. The switch waits for writes in progress. A server or worker that does not have this key refuses writes until it is redeployed with it. The worker then rewraps existing rows.
dataKey.promoted: Writers switched to the new key.
dataKey.heartbeatsAdvisory: Advisory only: processes report the key ids they hold every 30 seconds.
dataKey.heartbeatsNone: No process has reported in the last two minutes.

returnKeys.title: Return keys
returnKeys.none: No return key yet. The first host to connect creates one.
returnKeys.rotateDescription: Hosts get a new key to seal login captures to. The current key is retired and still opens captures sealed before the switch.
returnKeys.blockingCapped: More than {{count}} hosts still block destruction
returnKeys.destroyDescription: The private key is erased for good. Captures sealed to it can never be opened again.
returnKeys.destroyQuarantinedDescription_one: The private key is erased for good. {{count}} quarantined capture is sealed to it and can never be opened again.
returnKeys.destroyQuarantinedDescription_other: The private key is erased for good. {{count}} quarantined captures are sealed to it and can never be opened again.
returnKeys.destroyPrompt: Type the key id to confirm
returnKeys.ackedAt: Acked a newer key {{at}}; waiting for a drained report
returnKeys.notAcked: Has not acked a newer key
returnKeys.declareLostDescription: Host {{host}} will never reconnect, so it no longer blocks destroying {{kid}}. Captures it still holds under that key are lost. This cannot be undone.

refusals.not_configured: DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set on this server.
refusals.kid_malformed: That is not a valid key id.
refusals.key_not_held: This server does not hold that key. Deploy it first (as DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS).
refusals.not_initialized: There is no return key yet.
refusals.not_found: That key or host no longer exists.
refusals.current: The current return key cannot be destroyed. Rotate first.
refusals.host_not_drained: A host has not yet confirmed it no longer needs this key. Wait for it, or declare it lost.
refusals.quarantined_envelopes: Quarantined captures are sealed to this key. Refresh and confirm again.
refusals.already_declared: That host is already declared lost.
refusals.confirmation_mismatch: The typed key id does not match.
refusals.stale: This server does not hold the current data key. Retry after it is redeployed.
refusals.generic: The key action failed. Try again.
